subject: Urgent: HarborWave AZ3 fanout / regional routing failure — exec sync + credit request
messages:
From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@harborwave.io>
To: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: HarborWave Ops <ops@harborwave.io>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 29 Jul 2028 21:45:00 +0000
Subject: Production errors + latency spike in us-east-az3 (affecting checkout)

Hi Jonas —

We started seeing a sharp increase in 5xx rates and token-level latency at ~20:30 UTC for requests routed to us-east-az3. Impact: checkout flows for a subset of customers are timing out or returning 502s (about 18% of requests to that AZ). Our ops team auto-routed some traffic to us-east-az2 but the latency variability is causing significant errors on our side.

We urgently need temporary routing guidance and confirmation on whether Redwood can accept a geo-swap for this account (they're on reserved capacity in us-east). Also, HarborWave is asking for a short-term credit for the minutes impacted — they flagged revenue-sensitive traffic.

Attaching a quick KPI snapshot and a condensed error trace.

—Sam
Ops, HarborWave

Attachments: kpi-snapshot.csv, az3-error-trace.txt

From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@harborwave.io>, HarborWave Ops <ops@harborwave.io>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 29 Jul 2028 21:57:12 +0000
Subject: Re: Production errors + latency spike in us-east-az3 (affecting checkout)

Sam — thank you for the signal and the artifacts. We're taking this P0.

Short status:
- I've opened an internal incident (PagerDuty PDT-20280730-87) and asked infra to evaluate kernel-level saturation and KV cache pressure for models pinned to HarborWave's pool.
- Hannah: can you confirm whether Dedicated pool for HW is using preemptible nodes? If so, we'll coordinate an immediate drain and failover to warm capacity.
- Rishi: please evaluate cross-region routing options (pin fallback to us-east-az2 or us-west failover) and expected RPS/latency delta.

Sam: two asks for HarborWave ops while we triage: (1) hold any automated retries client-side for 15 minutes (they amplify QPS); (2) share an example request-id from a 502 so we can trace into logs.

I'll schedule an exec sync in 30 minutes if the impact persists — want leadership looped for any customer credit ask.

— Jonas
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 29 Jul 2028 22:10:03 +0000
Subject: Re: Production errors + latency spike in us-east-az3 (affecting checkout)

Adding commercial / escalation context. HarborWave is a top-10 monthly commit for our east region. If this affects their checkouts for more than an hour, they'll escalate to Finance and ask for a credit. They also have an ongoing procurement review (deal HW-ACCT-4123).

Marissa — Head of Sales Ops

Action items:
- I will join the incident bridge if we need a customer-facing readout and to fast-track a credit proposal.
- Stephanie: prepare the draft credit options (percentage-of-usage or fixed-dollar) so we can present something in the exec sync.

Please keep me posted on ETA for routing change and any impact window estimates.

From: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 29 Jul 2028 22:24:40 +0000
Subject: Re: Production errors + latency spike in us-east-az3 (affecting checkout)

Quick infra update from the bridge:
- Observed KV cache churn correlated with a model rollout that started ~20:15 UTC; warm caches on az3 were evicted faster than expected due to a spike in sequence lengths. Memory pressure triggered heavier host GC and a small kernel fallback that increased tail latency and 502s.
- We're pausing the rollout on az3 and starting an expedited drain of non-blocking pools (target: reduce inbound qps to az3 by ~70% over the next 20 mins).
- No signs of disk or NIC saturation; this is in-memory/throughput boundary.

Rishi is drafting routing rules now (policy: prefer existing region, fail to az2, then west).

Hannah
Principal Infra Eng, Serving Runtime

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 30 Jul 2028 00:02:15 +0000
Subject: Routing decision + customer impact estimate

Team — routing change applied at 23:52 UTC:
- Policy: traffic for HarborWave (account tag HW-4123) now routes to us-east-az2 for any node that would have selected az3; we left small sticky windows for in-flight tokens.
- Expected delta: +8–12ms median latency for HarborWave, occasional cold-KV tail spikes on first few requests after switch; estimated reduction of 5xxs to <1% within 10 minutes.
- We notified load balancer owners to hold sticky session TTL to 30s to avoid amplifying cold starts.

Estimated customer-visible downtime: effective mitigation started ~23:52 UTC; manifest successes observed by 00:05 UTC. HarborWave ops reported a drop from ~18% 5xx to ~0.8% by 00:06.

I recommend a post-mortem to look at rollout gating and a temporary runtime knob to throttle long-sequence-heavy inflight requests during model swaps.

— Rishi
Senior SRE, Serving

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@harborwave.io>, Julia Ramos <julia.ramos@harborwave.io>, HarborWave Ops <ops@harborwave.io>
Cc: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Jul 2028 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Redwood incident summary & proposed credit — HarborWave (HW-ACCT-4123)

Sam / Julia —

Thanks again for flagging this quickly and for the patience while our infra team mitigated the issue. Summary:
- Root cause: rollout-triggered KV cache churn on us-east-az3 increased host GC and produced a tail-latency amplification that translated to 502s for a subset of requests pinned to Dedicated pools.
- Mitigation: we paused the rollout on az3 and applied a routing policy to steer HarborWave traffic to az2 at 23:52 UTC; error rate reduced to <1% by 00:06 UTC on 2028-07-30.
- Customer impact window: ~20:30 UTC — 00:06 UTC (~3.5 hours), with highest error spike between 20:45–23:50 UTC.

Proposed commercial remedy (open for discussion):
- One-time credit equal to 20% of July usage for HW-ACCT-4123 billed portion that hit az3 during the incident window, or a flat $45,000 credit — whichever is larger.
- One-month elevated support window: white-glove SRE on-call for migration and rollout testing.

Attachments: proposed-credit-draft.pdf (detailed calculations)

Next steps:
1) Please confirm receipt and whether HarborWave would prefer the percentage or flat credit.
2) We will schedule a joint post-mortem and a rollout/gating workshop next week.

— Marissa
Head of Sales Ops, Redwood Inference
